newsitem.title: Estonia: Estonian government on verge of collapse.
newsitem.headline: Estonian government on verge of collapse.

text.p: The coalition government of the Baltic state of Estonia was on the verge of collapse on Wednesday after six ministers from the junior government partner announced their resignation.

The coalition was plunged into crisis after Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi signed a co-operation deal with the leading opposition party, infuriating his coalition partners from the Reform Party and sparking the resignations.
The coalition between the Coalition and Reform Parties is the sixth since Estonia, smallest of the three Baltic states, regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991.
The resignations were announced in an open letter to Vaehi, who still has to formally approve them.
The Reform Party gave Vaehi a Wednesday afternoon deadline to scrap the deal with the opposition Centre Party but he failed to comply.
The Reform Party itself will decide on Thursday whether to quit the government, which includes a smaller bloc of rural parties.
The group of ministers resigning includes Foreign Minister and Reform Party leader Siim Kallas.

"Tomorrow the Reform Party council will decide whether the party will continue in the coalition but already today we have made the conclusion for ourselves that we cannot continue in the government led by you," the letter to Vaehi said.
Vaehi has refused to cancel the pact with the Centre Party and has tried to reassure his partners that the deal would not lead to the Centre Party joining the coalition.

"If the Reform Party sticks to its position that new members, in this case the Centre Party, are not to be included in the governing coalition, then the Coalition Party will agree to this," the prime minister told a news conference.
He said his party would send a letter to the Reformists by the Wednesday deadline to explain its position.
The Reformists were angered by a clause in the co-operation deal which said Vaehi's party would work to include the Centre Party in the coalition.
Vaehi insisted that the Coalition and Centre parties would simply work together to "strengthen democracy".
The previous government was a Coalition/Centre partnership which collapsed amid scandal after the Centre Party leader was found to have taped confidential conversations.
Estonia, deemed one of the most successful reformers in eastern Europe, has managed to keep on a steady path of reform despite frequent political turmoil.
